patches.value: Source flow assertions on the normalized 2*pi torus, in mean-zero homogeneous spaces: for real mean-zero initial datum q, define U_t=U*U_x+U_xxx and its twist y_k(t)=exp(i*t*k^3)hat U(t,k), satisfying y'_k=(i*k/2)sum_{r+s=k}exp(3*i*k*r*s*t)y_r*y_s. (i) For sigma>=0, horizon b>0, and ||q||_2<=B0, the Galerkin approximations with nonlinearity projected onto |k|<=m are uniformly bounded in L^infty([0,b];dot H^sigma) by A_sigma depending only on sigma,b,B0,||q||_(dot H^sigma). (ii) If sigma>0 and 0<rho<sigma, a subsequence converges strongly in L^p([0,b];H^rho), every fixed 1<p<infinity, and weak-* in L^infty dot H^sigma to a coefficientwise integral solution with the same bound and ||y(t)||_2=||q||_2 a.e.. (iii) That solution is unique, is in C([0,b];dot H^sigma), conserves L^2 for every time, and depends Lipschitz continuously on initial data in dot H^sigma: for sigma>1/2 the constant may depend on sigma,b and the two initial dot H^sigma norms; for 0<sigma<=1/2 the continuity and uniqueness assertions hold with the same indicated topology. For sigma=0 there is a unique C([0,b];dot H^0) solution obtained by smooth approximation, Lipschitz in its data. (iv) For -1<theta<=0, any two such flows whose initial L^2 norms sum to at most B0 satisfy sup_[0,b]||y-z||_(dot H^theta)<=C'(B0,theta)*C_(B0,theta)^b*||y(0)-z(0)||_(dot H^theta). The same norm statements hold for U by the Fourier twist.
